title: Projection formulas for the fibre of a split difference map
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and $D(\mathcal A)$ its ordinary derived category with cohomology functors $H^q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let
$$G\xrightarrow{f}X\oplus Y\xrightarrow{d}Z\longrightarrow G[1]$$
be a distinguished triangle and put $p=\operatorname{pr}_X\circ f$ and $q=\operatorname{pr}_Y\circ f$. If $Z=Y$ and $d=(h,-1_Y)$ for a morphism $h:X\to Y$, then $p:G\to X$ is an isomorphism and $q=h\circ p$. For every integer $n$, $H^n(d)$ is a split epimorphism and $H^n(f)$ identifies $H^n(G)$ with the graph subobject $\ker H^n(d)$ of $H^n(X)\oplus H^n(Y)$, namely the image of $(1,H^n(h))$. Dually, if $Z=X$ and $d=(1_X,-r)$ for $r:Y\to X$, then $q:G\to Y$ is an isomorphism and $p=r\circ q$; $H^n(d)$ is a split epimorphism and $H^n(f)$ identifies $H^n(G)$ with the image of $(H^n(r),1)$ in $H^n(X)\oplus H^n(Y)$. These assertions remain valid after specified isomorphisms identifying the vertices and arrow of a distinguished triangle with either displayed form.

source.place: Tag 08DG (lemma-glue), split restriction calculation extracted as an abstract derived-category assertion; Tag 05RS (lemma-cohomology-homological).

proof.text: For d=(h,-1), conjugate the explicit section (0,-1) by the specified vertex isomorphisms: s=γ.hom ≫ (-biprod.inr) ≫ β.inv. For d=(1,-r), use s=γ.hom ≫ biprod.inl ≫ β.inv. In each case the arrow-identification hypothesis proves s ≫ T.mor₂ = 1. Hence the second triangle arrow is split epic and epic. Mathlib Triangle.mor₃_eq_zero_of_epi₂ gives T.mor₃=0, and Triangle.mono₁ makes T.mor₁ monic.

source.place: Tag 08DG, lemma-glue, restriction triangle and its split second arrow; Tag 05RS, lemma-cohomology-homological, and Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic

proof.text: Apply the triangle identity T.mor₁ ≫ T.mor₂=0 from [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact]. After composing with γ.hom and using the prescribed β-identification, expand the biproduct difference map. The two cases give q=p≫h and p=q≫r respectively. Thus fβ=p≫j in the first case with j=(1,h), and fβ=q≫j in the second case with j=(r,1).

source.place: Tag 08DG, lemma-glue, restriction triangle and its split second arrow; Tag 05RS, lemma-cohomology-homological, and Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic

proof.text: For either case, let π be the appropriate projection and j its graph section, so j≫π=1. The composite j≫β.inv is killed by T.mor₂. By Triangle.coyoneda_exact₂ in [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], obtain k with k≫T.mor₁=j≫β.inv; consequently k≫T.mor₁≫β.hom=j. Then k≫(T.mor₁≫β.hom≫π)=j≫π=1. Conversely, (T.mor₁≫β.hom≫π)≫k≫T.mor₁≫β.hom=(T.mor₁≫β.hom≫π)≫j=T.mor₁≫β.hom. Cancel the monomorphism T.mor₁≫β.hom to prove the other inverse identity. This constructs the required projection isomorphism directly in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 08DG, lemma-glue, restriction triangle and its split second arrow; Tag 05RS, lemma-cohomology-homological, and Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic

proof.text: For F=H^n, functoriality preserves the constructed splitting of T.mor₂, so F(T.mor₂) is split epic. Since the appropriate projection p or q is now an isomorphism, F(p) or F(q) is monic; its factorization through F(T.mor₁) implies that F(T.mor₁) is monic. Check the two projections of F(T.mor₁≫β.hom)≫Functor.biprodComparison F X Y: using functoriality and the already proved component equality, it is F(p)≫(1,F(h)) or F(q)≫(F(r),1). Precomposition by the isomorphism F(p) or F(q) does not change an image subobject (imageSubobject_iso_comp), giving the asserted graph-image equality.

source.place: Tag 08DG, lemma-glue, restriction triangle and its split second arrow; Tag 05RS, lemma-cohomology-homological, and Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic

proof.text: In any abelian category the graph j=(1,a) is split monic with retraction pr₁, and j≫(a,-1)=0. Therefore its image subobject is Subobject.mk j and factors through the kernel subobject. For the reverse inclusion, let t be the kernel-subobject arrow. The equation t≫(a,-1)=0 gives t≫pr₂=t≫pr₁≫a; hence t=(t≫pr₁)≫j. The two factorizations give equality of the graph image and the kernel subobject. For j=(b,1) and difference map (1,-b), use retraction pr₂ and the equation t≫pr₁=t≫pr₂≫b instead. Apply these calculations to a=H^n(h) and b=H^n(r), and combine with the preceding image equalities. No cohomological detection or long exact sequence is needed.

lean.statement: theorem split_fibre_projections (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory A)) (hT : T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory A)) (X Y : DerivedCategory A) (β : T.obj₂ ≅ X ⊞ Y) : (∀ (h : X ⟶ Y) (γ : T.obj₃ ≅ Y), T.mor₂ ≫ γ.hom = β.hom ≫ biprod.desc h (-𝟙 Y) → IsIso (T.mor₁ ≫ β.hom ≫ biprod.fst) ∧ T.mor₁ ≫ β.hom ≫ biprod.snd = (T.mor₁ ≫ β.hom ≫ biprod.fst) ≫ h ∧ ∀ n : ℤ, IsSplitEpi ((homologyFunctor A n).map T.mor₂) ∧ Mono ((homologyFunctor A n).map T.mor₁) ∧ imageSubobject ((homologyFunctor A n).map (T.mor₁ ≫ β.hom) ≫ Functor.biprodComparison (homologyFunctor A n) X Y) = kernelSubobject (biprod.desc ((homologyFunctor A n).map h) (-𝟙 ((homologyFunctor A n).obj Y))) ∧ imageSubobject ((homologyFunctor A n).map (T.mor₁ ≫ β.hom) ≫ Functor.biprodComparison (homologyFunctor A n) X Y) = imageSubobject (biprod.lift (𝟙 ((homologyFunctor A n).obj X)) ((homologyFunctor A n).map h))) ∧ (∀ (r : Y ⟶ X) (γ : T.obj₃ ≅ X), T.mor₂ ≫ γ.hom = β.hom ≫ biprod.desc (𝟙 X) (-r) → IsIso (T.mor₁ ≫ β.hom ≫ biprod.snd) ∧ T.mor₁ ≫ β.hom ≫ biprod.fst = (T.mor₁ ≫ β.hom ≫ biprod.snd) ≫ r ∧ ∀ n : ℤ, IsSplitEpi ((homologyFunctor A n).map T.mor₂) ∧ Mono ((homologyFunctor A n).map T.mor₁) ∧ imageSubobject ((homologyFunctor A n).map (T.mor₁ ≫ β.hom) ≫ Functor.biprodComparison (homologyFunctor A n) X Y) = kernelSubobject (biprod.desc (𝟙 ((homologyFunctor A n).obj X)) (-((homologyFunctor A n).map r))) ∧ imageSubobject ((homologyFunctor A n).map (T.mor₁ ≫ β.hom) ≫ Functor.biprodComparison (homologyFunctor A n) X Y) = imageSubobject (biprod.lift ((homologyFunctor A n).map r) (𝟙 ((homologyFunctor A n).obj Y))))
